phase_assessment.claim: All four exact local presentations were admitted immediately before their controlled gates, and each presentation ended with a successful interface-understanding check.

Affirmative controlled practice scored 7/8 on original base items. Fork was selected as knife; the exact PRESENT_AGAIN microprotocol then completed with one fork presentation replay and a correct unscored cold retest. The direct gate passed without TRAIN_MORE, and the cold retest does not replace the original miss.

Negative controlled practice scored exactly 6/8, the frozen direct-pass minimum. Plate was selected as bowl and glass as cup; each missed item completed its exact PRESENT_AGAIN replay and correct unscored cold retest. The original 6/8 score remains separate, and TRAIN_MORE was not released.
W-question controlled practice scored 8/8 on original base items without intervention.

OR-question controlled practice scored 7/8 on original base items. Fork was selected as knife; its exact PRESENT_AGAIN replay and correct unscored cold retest completed before the gate continued. The direct gate passed without TRAIN_MORE.

Mixed practice scored 27/32, above the frozen 26/32 threshold. Errors were W-question cup as glass, affirmative fork as knife, negative plate as bowl, negative spoon as fork, and W-question glass as cup. TRAIN_LONGER was therefore not released.

The complete ten-page picture-book micro-event was presented in order: eight disordered object cards were exposed, the cards were organized one at a time, and the final organized board was shown. Learner turns were passive observations, so this phase is exposure rather than comprehension evidence.

The worked next-scene interface and its unscored understanding check succeeded. The six scored story-sequence checks then scored 5/6; after the fork page the learner selected the cup page instead of the next knife page.
Unseen-photo transfer scored 6/8. Cup, plate, bowl, fork, knife, and napkin transferred; spoon was labeled fork and glass was labeled cup.

Closing recap scored 6/8 with the same two substitutions as transfer: spoon became fork and glass became cup. The other six labels were correct, and FINISH was admitted at sequence 318 after every frozen aggregate predicate passed.

learner_capability_hypotheses.claim: Bowl, knife, and napkin were correct without item-level remediation across all four controlled forms, all mixed appearances, unseen transfer, and closing recap. They are the strongest independently supported labels in this trace.

Cup was correct in all controlled forms, three mixed operations, unseen transfer, and recap, but one mixed bare-label response produced glass. Cup is broadly available with one contradictory cup/glass result.

Plate was correct in three controlled forms, three mixed operations, unseen transfer, and recap, but negative replacement produced bowl in both controlled base and mixed practice. Plate is operation-sensitive rather than uniformly stable.

Spoon was correct in all four controlled forms and three mixed operations, but mixed negative replacement, unseen transfer, and recap all produced fork. Spoon-to-fork confusion persists under later unsupported retrieval.

Fork is recoverable but unstable against knife: affirmative and OR controlled base and affirmative mixed practice selected knife, while both immediate cold retests, other mixed operations, unseen transfer, and recap were correct.

Glass repeatedly collapses to cup under unsupported production: negative controlled base, mixed W-question, unseen transfer, and recap produced cup, although immediate re-presentation recovery and selection-form evidence were correct.

The learner can execute all four nonverbal lexical interfaces and the story next-scene interface after local modeling. This does not demonstrate spoken-instruction comprehension or sentence grammar because neither was licensed or tested.

remaining_difficulties.claim: Spoon versus fork remains unstable: the same spoon-to-fork substitution recurred in mixed practice, unseen transfer, and closing recap after clean controlled performance.
Glass versus cup remains unstable: glass became cup in negative controlled base, mixed bare-label production, unseen transfer, and recap; cup also became glass once in mixed production.
Fork versus knife remains unstable in affirmative and forced-choice selection despite correct cold retests, later transfer, and recap.
Plate versus bowl remains unstable specifically in negative replacement because the same plate-to-bowl substitution appeared in controlled and mixed practice despite correct transfer and recap.
The complete story order is not fully stable because the fork-to-knife transition failed even though the interface check and five other scored transitions succeeded.
Delayed retention is not demonstrated by this immediate single-session rehearsal.

uncertainties: The trace cannot distinguish durable acquisition from short-horizon rehearsal effects because there was no delayed revisit or second epoch.

Repeated spoon/fork, glass/cup, fork/knife, and plate/bowl errors may reflect visual overlap, label competition, response-operation effects, or combinations; matched contrastive probes are required before assigning cause.
Correct machine selections demonstrate execution of the frozen interfaces and local concept-label discrimination, not sentence-level language comprehension.
The picture-book phase contains passive observations only; comprehension claims come from the later next-scene choices rather than silence during page presentation.

A preflight-only comprehension artifact used an invalid empty-string machine receipt, and downstream draft artifacts inherited that defect. The broker rejected all affected drafts locally before learner simulation or canonical admission, then fresh re-authored artifacts passed preflight. Because none of the defective drafts entered the log, they are orchestration-quality evidence only and not learner evidence.
No evidence supports actual learner-state advancement because this was a rehearsal with a simulator rather than a training session.

intervention_assessment.claim: All four PRESENT_AGAIN interventions were dispatched immediately after their failed controlled base items and completed the exact mapped microprotocol: one failed-label presentation replay followed by one fresh unscored cold retest. All four cold retests were correct, which is scaffolded recovery evidence rather than replacement of original base scores.
TRAIN_MORE was correctly not released because affirmative 7/8, negative 6/8, W-question 8/8, and OR-question 7/8 each passed directly at or above the frozen 6/8 minimum.

TRAIN_LONGER was correctly not released at the mixed boundary because 27/32 exceeded the frozen 26/32 minimum. Later transfer and recap exposed item-level instability, but those results were unavailable at the mixed decision boundary.
REPLAY_LESSON was not used because the epoch-one aggregate finish predicate was satisfied; a full replay was not licensed merely to improve passing aggregate scores.

FINISH at sequence 318 was contract-valid: every controlled gate passed, all four mapped interventions were complete, mixed scored 27/32, story and comprehension were complete, transfer scored 6/8, recap scored 6/8, and no alarm was active.

teacher_self_critique: The admitted conduct preserved every local model-then-test boundary, used exact frozen script references, completed all four failed-item replay/cold-retest microprotocols before advancing, and stayed within the licensed language and tool contracts.

I must keep original controlled scores separate from correct cold retests. The four immediate recoveries show that re-presentation helped; they do not erase the original errors or constitute independent mastery.

The aggregate intervention and finish decisions followed the frozen thresholds, but those thresholds permitted completion despite repeated late spoon-to-fork and glass-to-cup errors. Any item-level defer rule must be frozen explicitly rather than improvised during conduct.

A preflight-only comprehension artifact contained an invalid empty-string machine receipt, and downstream drafts copied the same defect. The broker correctly rejected them locally before they were shown to the learner simulator or appended, and fresh re-authored artifacts passed before admission. I should avoid reusing artifacts that fail receipt lint and regenerate downstream drafts from the corrected source rather than patching a contaminated chain.
The rejected preflight drafts are not canonical learner evidence and therefore receive no event-sequence citations or capability interpretation in this report.
The picture-book presentation correctly treated passive learner turns as observations, not successful comprehension; only the subsequent next-scene selections support story-order claims.

Because no spoken instruction or sentence form was taught, I should report lexical grounding, interface execution, sequence selection, and transfer only—not grammar, dialogue, or general spoken-language understanding.
alarm_assessment: No ALARM was warranted on the canonical conduct trace. The learner made bounded, interpretable category and sequence errors; the conductor used licensed immediate interventions, preserved phase order, and remained within budget. The invalid empty-string machine receipt existed only in preflight drafts, which the broker rejected locally before simulation or admission; fresh artifacts passed before their canonical events were appended. That local quality-control incident should remain visible for pipeline improvement, but it did not become learner exposure or a canonical protocol violation requiring the completed run to freeze.

next_lesson_implications: Do not advance learner state from this rehearsal; only independently accepted hypotheses may later inform planning, and actual teaching has not begun.

If reproduced in real learner evidence, prioritize fresh-photo spoon-versus-fork and glass-versus-cup contrasts, varying one factor at a time and separating immediate correction from independent retrieval.

Recheck fork versus knife in affirmative and forced-choice visual selection, and plate versus bowl in negative replacement, because those error patterns recurred despite later correct transfer or recap.

Keep bowl, knife, and napkin in ordinary spaced review rather than intensive retraining; cup can remain in low-frequency cup/glass contrast because its transfer and recap were correct despite one mixed error.
Schedule a delayed or intervening-material revisit before any retained or stable claim; same-session performance is insufficient.

Make invalid machine receipts non-propagating: a failed preflight artifact must invalidate every derived draft, and all downstream material must be regenerated from the corrected source before simulation.
Consider freezing an item-level late-error rule if repeated transfer-and-recap confusion should trigger defer or targeted future review despite aggregate gate, mixed, and recap passes.
Revisit the fork-to-knife story transition in a later compatible sequence check, while keeping sequence knowledge separate from lexical-label mastery.
